A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the resistance mechanism in O. nubilaris is due to a loss in the ability of the midgut epithelium to translocate the toxin to the cytosol, not a loss of binding.
Cry1Ab binding is not altered in resistant larvae and that resistance is not associated with reduced binding of Cry1Ac.
the resistance to Cry1Ac is associated with a reduction in midgut membrane permeability, while resistance to Cry1Ba is associated with a decrease in the rate of toxin translocation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Cry1Ac binding proteins in the Bt-resistant O. nubilis are not different in number or binding affinity than the Cry1Ac proteins found in the Bt-susceptible O. nubili.
Cry1Ab toxin binding to the midgut membrane of Bt-resistant O. nubalalis larvae is similar to that of susceptible larvae.
the binding assays used here can be used to compare binding of Bt toxins to membranes from resistant and susceptible insects.
